clue.text: Perhaps cricket clubs attracted by class on batting

indicators.note: in an across clue, 'on' means coming after, so the following piece is placed behind the earlier one

parts.note: a cricket side that is batting is said to be in

indicators.note: something attracted by another is drawn into it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a set is a class or group, as in a school set
C is the card-game abbreviation for the clubs suit

explanation.surface: Cricket clubs drawing in new members thanks to their classy batting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all about the sport, but 'cricket' is the chirping creature. Batting sides are 'in' at cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is one example of the six-legged creatures, signalled by 'Perhaps', which marks an example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Greek character in chinos juggling to such an extent

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it
juggled items are tossed about and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man in chinos performing a juggling act, to a remarkable degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' sounds like a person wearing the trousers, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and the trousers supply only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomuch is a formal adverb meaning to such a degree, usually followed by 'that' or 'as'.

clue.text: Ask queen shortly to mingle — Duke's informed

indicators.note: cut short, so the final letter is dropped
things that mingle mix together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the word with its last letter removed
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go and chat with the Queen at a party, and the Duke has been tipped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Informed' looks like 'knowledgeable', but it is the past tense of informing on someone; ASK mixed with QUEE gives SQUEAKE, and D finishes SQUEAKED.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeak, like to squeal, is slang for betraying secrets to the police or authorities.

clue.text: Senior officer half-concealed load on wharf without a conversation

indicators.note: if half of a word is concealed, only the other half remains visible
'without' means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
the first half of the word, the second half being hidden
a quay is a landing stage or wharf
the letter that leaves the wharf

explanation.surface: An officer partly hiding a cargo on the dockside, without a word to anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the A from QUAY leaves QUY, which completes COL + LO + QUY.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquy is a formal word for a talk or dialogue between people, especially a learned discussion.

clue.text: Following drink, seaman's given biscuit

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
to lap is to drink, as a cat does
Jack, or Jack Tar, is a traditional name for a sailor

explanation.surface: After a drink, a sailor is handed a biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a flapjack is a chewy oat bar made with butter and golden syrup, not the American pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: The British flapjack is a baked oat-and-syrup tray bake, loosely counted among biscuits or cookies.

clue.text: Discussed meadow and footpath margin

indicators.note: what is discussed is spoken, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow
a way is a path or track

explanation.surface: Talking over a field and the strip of path at its edge.
explanation.walkthrough: LEA and LEE sound the same; the path word is already spelt right.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room for manoeuvre or tolerance, a spare allowance that works as a safety margin.

clue.text: Usually Italians are here every year collecting fruit

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it up and hold it

parts.note: p.a. stands for per annum, Latin for each year
the ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo hybrid

explanation.surface: Italians are typically found here annually, picking fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic description: the place where you would normally expect Italians to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Puglia, also called Apulia, is the region forming the heel of Italy, so its people are mostly Italian.

clue.text: Ornamental shrub unknown porter maybe carried through two acres

indicators.note: whatever is carried through something sits inside it from one side to the other

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for acre, taken twice
z is an algebraic unknown
porter is a dark beer, an example of ale

explanation.surface: A garden bush being taken across two acres by an anonymous delivery man.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'porter' a carrier; here it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Azaleas are flowering shrubs of the rhododendron family grown in gardens for their showy blooms.

clue.text: Emperor's spirit lives on in retirement

parts.note: in ancient Egyptian belief the ka is a person's spiritual double
to live is to be, so lives gives the verb form is

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so in a down clue the letters run upward

parts.note: re means on or about, as in the subject line of a letter

explanation.surface: A former emperor's soul lingers on after he steps down.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the final piece goes backwards; the spirit and 'lives' read straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaiser was the title of the German and Austrian emperors, derived from the Roman name Caesar.

clue.text: Court game is declined by mum and learners in brief storm

indicators.note: what is declined is turned down and refused, so letters are dropped

parts.note: squash is a racket game played on an indoor court
keeping mum means keeping quiet, as in 'sh!'
L is the learner-driver plate, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Mother and the novices turn down a game of squash during a short storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother, but it is the call for silence. L-plates mark learner drivers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A squall is a sudden violent gust or short-lived burst of wind, often bringing rain.

clue.text: Mountain soldier describes mist briefly in North Africa

definitions.note: names the place by where it is, standing for a city there

indicators.note: to describe is also to trace around, as in describing a circle, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
a GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: haze is a light mist

explanation.surface: A mountain trooper reports a brief fog in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describes' sounds like reporting, but is the geometric sense of drawing round.
explanation.definitionFit: Benghazi is the second city of Libya, a port on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa.

clue.text: Gerard regularly comes in to cut field

indicators.note: coming into something means going inside it

parts.note: to mow is to cut grass

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the name

explanation.surface: Gerard turns up on a regular basis to mow a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Gerard looks like a farmhand; he is only a source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a grassy field, especially one left to grow hay, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Part of poem written in vulgar language

indicators.note: words written in something are placed inside it

parts.note: base means coarse or low
a poem is made up of lines

explanation.surface: A section of verse composed in crude, rude words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vulgar language' reads as one phrase meaning swearing; the definition is the last word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Balinese is the Austronesian tongue spoken on the Indonesian island of Bali.

clue.text: What faces British topless steeplechaser?

indicators.note: without a top, so the head letter is removed

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a harrier is a cross-country runner, and runners in the steeplechase event are of that kind

explanation.surface: What confronts a bare-chested British runner in a steeplechase?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and the whole clue builds: a steeplechase runner confronts hurdles, and B plus a beheaded harrier gives one.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechase is run over fixed hurdles and a water jump, each an obstacle in the runner's path.

clue.text: One tweets the tenth character

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a noisy bird of the crow family
second meaning: the spelt-out name of a letter of the alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweets' suggests social media posts, but it is birdsong; 'character' is a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The jay is a colourful songbird that calls, and J, spelt jay, is the alphabet's tenth letter.

clue.text: Using teeth, damage drinking vessel — shape is retained within

indicators.note: something retained within is held inside

parts.note: a cup is a vessel for drinking
to hew is to cut into shape, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Biting into a mug and damaging it, its form still held inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase, 'damage using teeth', reordered to open the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To chew something up is to destroy or mangle it by biting, as a dog does with a slipper.

clue.text: Disease coming from foreign river? Wrong

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a cross marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: An illness picked up from an overseas river, though apparently mistakenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' at the end looks like a comment on the surface; it is the X of a marked mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Pox is a general name for diseases causing pustules, such as smallpox or chickenpox.

clue.text: Cleaner's way of working quietly

parts.note: MO stands for modus operandi, Latin for method of operating
p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A cleaner's habit of going about their job without noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like a person; it is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A mop is a long-handled implement with absorbent strands used for washing floors.

clue.text: I accept that Euro when abroad in distant environment

indicators.note: an environment is the surroundings, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: yon is an old word for distant, as in yonder

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller agreeing to take euros while overseas in a far-off place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' reads as travel, but here means scrambled; the currency letters sit inside YON.
explanation.definitionFit: "You're on" is a colloquial way of accepting a bet or challenge, agreeing to take it up.

clue.text: Sail raised, Russian man approached channel

indicators.note: a thing that approaches another comes right up next to it
in a down clue raising something sends its letters upward, from bottom to top

parts.note: Ivan is a typical Russian man's name
a gate can be a channel, such as the passage through which molten metal enters a mould

explanation.surface: With sail hoisted, a Russian came up to the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sail raised' reads as one phrase, but the comma is a decoy: 'Sail' is the definition and 'raised' goes with the Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: To navigate is to steer a course over water, and to sail is likewise to travel by boat.

clue.text: Old prince somewhat open with an amateur actor getting all upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so in a down clue the whole string is turned upside down

parts.note: a door that is ajar is slightly open
the indefinite article
a ham is an overacting or amateurish performer

explanation.surface: An elderly royal with his door slightly open, losing his temper at a bad actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All' tells you the whole string is turned, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharaja was a great ruling prince of an Indian state before independence, hence 'old'.

clue.text: Iron velvety material right away in rented property

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a let is a property rented out

indicators.note: something sent away is gone, so a letter leaves

parts.note: velour is a plush fabric resembling velvet
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Pressing a plush fabric correctly in a rented flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' looks like a noun or the laundry chore, but is a verb meaning flatten.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron something out is to flatten or smooth it, as does level out, making it even.

clue.text: Trim drinking promotion display

indicators.note: whatever is drinking takes something in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: to pare is to trim or cut away the edges
an ad is an advertisement, a promotion

explanation.surface: A sleek drinks-promotion stand at an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' suggests neat or slim; here it is the verb to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To parade is to show off conspicuously, and a parade is a public show or exhibition.

clue.text: Tread on someone's toes leaving terminus

parts.note: someone who is off is departing
a terminus is the end of a line

explanation.surface: Stepping on a fellow passenger's feet while getting off at the last stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an idiom, so the toes are figurative.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread on someone's toes is an idiom for upsetting or insulting them by intruding.

clue.text: Two unknowns supporting sporting occasion's collection of stars

indicators.note: in a down clue, what supports something sits beneath it

parts.note: a gala is a sports meeting, especially a swimming event
x and y are standard algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: A pair of nobodies backing a sports event's lineup of famous names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests celebrities; the definition wants the astronomical sense. A swimming gala is a common British school competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a vast system of millions of stars bound by gravity, and figuratively a dazzling assembly of celebrities.

clue.text: Public speaker once from the Magic Circle breaking rules

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for rule, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: magic transforms things, so these letters are conjured into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a circle is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A former orator expelled from the Magic Circle for breaching its code.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Circle is the famous British society of magicians, whose members must not reveal secrets; here 'Magic' and 'Circle' do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhetor was a teacher or master of rhetoric in ancient Greece and Rome, an orator of old.

clue.text: Something for the head chef? Some shiraz, at the end

indicators.note: points to the final position of each word, so only closing letters are kept

parts.note: the closing letter of the cook
the closing letter of the quantity word
the closing letter of the wine

explanation.surface: A gift for the head chef: a drop of shiraz at the end of service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head chef' looks like one phrase, but 'head' belongs to the definition and 'chef' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A fez is a flat-topped, brimless felt hat, usually red with a tassel, worn on the head.

clue.text: Bones those people commonly found in ancient marketplaces

indicators.note: something found in a place is located inside it

parts.note: fora is the Latin plural of forum, the Roman marketplace
'em is the informal, dropped-aitch form of them

explanation.surface: Skeletons of people unearthed in the old market squares of antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' signals casual speech, which clips them to 'em.
explanation.definitionFit: Femora is the Latin plural of femur, the thigh bone, the longest in the human body.

clue.text: Bird outside remains comparatively loud

indicators.note: one thing outside another wraps around it

parts.note: a flier is anything that flies, such as a bird
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A bird outdoors staying relatively noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud' here is about showy colours or clothes, not noise; 'remains' is a noun, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud can describe garish clothes or colours, and flashier means more ostentatious or gaudy.

clue.text: Face appearing to droop during fight

indicators.note: something happening during another falls within it

parts.note: to vie is to compete or contend
to sag is to droop

explanation.surface: A boxer's features seeming to sag mid-bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' reads as a verb, to confront, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Visage is a literary word for a person's face or facial expression.

clue.text: Rigorous one performing oppressive demand

parts.note: exact means precise and strict
the Roman numeral for one
a performer who is on is on stage

explanation.surface: A strict performer making harsh requests.
explanation.walkthrough: A performer is 'on' while on stage, a common crossword sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaction is the act of extorting payment, or a sum harshly and unfairly required, such as a heavy tax.

clue.text: Native American's certainly not consuming coffee — it's rejected

indicators.note: to consume something is to take it inside

parts.note: a firm refusal

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: java is slang for coffee, after the Indonesian island

explanation.surface: A Native American firmly refusing a cup of coffee and sending it back.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's 's is the contraction of 'is', so it reads 'Native American is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Navajo are a people of the south-western United States, the largest federally recognised tribe.

clue.text: Sat perhaps alongside Bill, entertaining Roger and Dawn

indicators.note: placed beside, so the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday, an example of a day

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest has them inside the house

parts.note: a bird's bill is its beak
in radio talk Roger stands for R, received

explanation.surface: Someone sat beside Bill while he hosted Roger and Dawn, as if at a dinner party.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill, Roger and Dawn all look like guests' names; only Dawn keeps that role as the definition, and Sat is Saturday, not seated.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is the first light of morning, when day breaks, the same moment as dawn.

clue.text: One across road accommodating European worker

definitions.note: a cross-reference to the answer at 1 across, which is defined by example

indicators.note: to accommodate someone is to give them room inside

parts.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road
E is the abbreviation for European
the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: Someone crossing a road and making room for a European labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One across' looks like a direction to walk over the road; it points to the 1 across answer, INSECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A red ant is a species of small reddish stinging ant, and every ant is an insect.
